headline: Computational navigation of large chemical spaces linking structure to bioactivity
label: Chemical Space Navigation Methods
summary: Ultralarge virtual libraries and make-on-demand spaces now demand scalable methods to locate activity cliffs and steer generative design.
synthesis: The dominant thread is computational navigation of large chemical spaces to connect molecular structure with bioactivity. BitBIRCH clustering is applied to large compound libraries to locate activity cliffs or delineate smooth regions. Ultralarge virtual libraries, framed as central to early-stage drug discovery, enable exploration of billions of compounds. M-FRAG aligns molecules and fragments in a shared embedding space to prioritize property-relevant fragments for RL-based generation. Another study applies DPO and DiffusionNFT reinforcement learning to pocket-conditioned generative models, steering structure-based molecules toward make-on-demand libraries such as Enamine REAL. What is new is the coupling of generative design to synthesizable library spaces rather than navigation alone. The items differ in method and validation design, so they reflect a shared orientation rather than a uniform finding.
